parole.significato: suffix appended to verbs to create nouns denoting act, state
parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Slavic *-znь. The spelling in the nominative case may have been influenced by Old Church Slavonic -знь (-znĭ), as -зень would probably be expected, compare Czech bázeň, Polish bojaźń, Serbo-Croatian бојазан, Slovene bojazen and Bulgarian боя́зън (bojázăn) exhibiting -zьnь while

parole.significato: font, baptismal font (a large basin with holy water used for baptism)
parole.testo: Inherited from Old Ruthenian кꙋпѣль (kupělʹ), from Old East Slavic кꙋпѣль (kupělĭ), from Proto-Slavic *kǫpělь. In the Christian context, a semantic loan from Old Church Slavonic кѫпѣль (kǫpělĭ, “font”). By surface analysis, купа́ти (kupáty) + -іль (-ilʹ).

parole.significato: to pamper, to coddle, to mollycoddle, to baby, to nurse
parole.testo: Inherited from Old Ruthenian пестовати (pestovati), from Proto-Slavic *pěstovati, "e" instead of "і" in the root is unexpected, possibly borrowed from Old Church Slavonic пѣстовати (pěstovati).

Inherited from Old East Slavic притъча (pritŭča, “incident”), from Proto-Slavic *pritъča (“incident, tale”). The meaning "tale" is likely a semantic loan from Old Church Slavonic притъча (pritŭča, “tale, parable”).

parole.significato: to torment, to torture, to anguish, to excruciate, to harrow
parole.testo: Inherited from Old East Slavic тьрзати (tĭrzati), from Proto-Slavic *tьrzati. Due to its literary nature, it was possibly borrowed from Old Church Slavonic трьзати (trĭzati).
